13_h.s_54: On Day 9, Clement Hs arrived during an argument about a missing spoon. The war already had matters more urgent than introductions.

Clement Hs was hit in the hand while passing a mug along the trench at R-C14. He did not spill a drop. The men are still talking about that. Shot by Konrad Nsrr of the Concord (@nsrr_007). Clement Hs walked the captured trenches of Blackwater Canal and found the enemy's cooking pots still warm. He took a spoon as a souvenir.

Clement Hs rejoined the squad at R-C14. Someone had written his name on the wall with 'still alive' under it. He left it there. The clerk counted the names twice. Clement Hs is number 913 of the first thousand to answer the call, and wears the ribbon of the First Thousand. The Hegemony flag went up over Grey Mill. Clement Hs did not cheer. He sat down on a sandbag and ate his ration slowly, like a man with time again.

Clement Hs fired one burst and pulled the gun down before the reply came. The reply hit empty sandbags. Konrad Nsrr did not get to reply at all, grazed. Clement Hs fired short bursts at the gap in the enemy wire, the way the sergeant taught. Pavel Hemana was badly wounded trying to cross it.
A grenade fragment found Clement Hs's shoulder. He calls it a souvenir and refuses to be sent back.
auxiliary_az: "You're late," said the corporal when Gideon Auxiliary arrived on Day 11. "Everyone's late. Get a spade." Grey Mill is in Hegemony hands. Gideon Auxiliary watched the map being corrected and wondered how such a small pencil mark could take so much work.

On sentry duty Gideon Auxiliary watched the wire for six hours. Twice he thought the wire watched back. A letter from home found Gideon Auxiliary before the night shift. Gideon Auxiliary folded it small and kept it close.

Gideon Auxiliary took stock of his pockets: string, crumbs, a pencil and no sign of the button he was looking for. A letter from home found Gideon Auxiliary before the night shift. Gideon Auxiliary folded it small and kept it close.
azhanselmc: Silas "Ash" Azhanselmc told the sergeant he was a carpenter. The sergeant said the war needed one of those like it needed a hole in the roof, and put him on sentry.

A periscope poked up from the enemy line. Silas "Ash" Azhanselmc shot it to pieces, and the man holding it, Bastian Passing, was grazed. News of the loss of Blackwater Canal reached T-F11 with the rations. Silas "Ash" Azhanselmc ate while listening to the revised orders.

Silas "Ash" Azhanselmc was hit in the knee while crossing a low part of the trench at T-F11. He will walk again, the medic thinks, but not soon. Shot by Walter "Bones" Boccadifuoco of the Hegemony (@boccadifuocoandrea). Day 11: Grey Mill was lost. Silas "Ash" Azhanselmc wrote down the news without trying to explain it.
Silas "Ash" Azhanselmc spent the day on a stretcher counting the bearers who went past. Forty-three. None of them stopped.
The medics would not give up on Silas "Ash" Azhanselmc. On a stretcher in the open, between salvos, they kept him alive and then kept him whole. He returned to T-F11 today.
carpet.floooring: Gustav "Brick" Floooring arrived on Day 4 and found the section asleep. The welcome had to wait until somebody needed the kettle.
Gustav "Brick" Floooring shaved using a spoon for a mirror. One side looks ready for inspection. The other looks ready for winter.

A bullet clipped Gustav "Brick" Floooring's helmet at R-F2 and took a strip of scalp with it. He bled into his collar, swore, and lay low. Shot by Rafael Davidsonmars of the Concord (@davidsonmarshall). The Hegemony flag went up over Hill 304. Gustav "Brick" Floooring did not cheer. He sat down on a sandbag and ate his ration slowly, like a man with time again.
Gustav "Brick" Floooring sat out the day with a bandaged arm, cleaning every rifle within reach. It was the only job the medic would allow.
The medics cleaned Gustav "Brick" Floooring's wound one last time and pronounced him fit. He is back to full duty at R-F2.
Gustav "Brick" Floooring fired short bursts at the gap in the enemy wire, the way the sergeant taught. Valentin Jarg was badly wounded trying to cross it.

Dawn watch. Gustav "Brick" Floooring put a round across no man's land and the enemy line went quiet: Hugo Luissantos, grazed. Gustav "Brick" Floooring was hit in the hand while passing a mug along the trench at R-F2. He did not spill a drop. The men are still talking about that. Shot by Rafael Davidsonmars of the Concord (@davidsonmarshall).

Gustav "Brick" Floooring was hit in the hip at R-F2. Two men dragged him along the trench floor to the nearest medic. Shot by Anselm Whispertooth of the Concord (@whispertooth). Gustav "Brick" Floooring was killed at R-F2 just after dawn. The cup of tea beside him was still hot. Shot by Anselm Whispertooth of the Concord (@whispertooth).
Jakub "Whistle" Floooring asked about Gustav "Brick" Floooring on arriving at R-F2. The first story concerned a stolen breakfast. He asked for another.

A child had slipped a riddle into a parcel for Jakub "Whistle" Floooring. He kept the dugout guessing until supper, then turned the page over and read the answer. The clerk counted the names twice. Jakub "Whistle" Floooring is number 305 of the first thousand to answer the call, and wears the ribbon of the First Thousand. News that the Hegemony had taken Grey Mill reached Jakub "Whistle" Floooring during supper. The same stew suddenly tasted better.

Machine-gun fire swept R-F2. Jakub "Whistle" Floooring took a round through the side and was carried back, grey in the face and very quiet. Shot by Bastian Mrbojo of the Concord (@mrbojo1992). Jakub "Whistle" Floooring stood up to fix a loose sandbag at R-F2. He did not get to finish the job. Shot by Bastian Mrbojo of the Concord (@mrbojo1992).
Wendel "Spark" Floooring put a frozen apple beside the bunk. Someone who had known Jakub "Whistle" Floooring helped clear the shelf without saying why.

Wendel "Spark" Floooring fired at the flash of a shovel across the wire. Behind the shovel was Henrik Bowles, now badly wounded. A bullet went through Wendel "Spark" Floooring's sleeve at R-F2 and took some skin with it. He kept the sleeve. Shot by Norbert Tsepnidiss of the Concord (@tsepnidiss._6).
christianbarefoot3440: Bastian Christianbar, a farmhand from Northwick, was sent forward on Day 5 to fill a gap in S-F1. The gap had a name once. Nobody says it.

A splinter opened Bastian Christianbar's cheek at S-F1. A medic stitched it on the spot and he was back on the fire step before the tea went cold. A letter from home found Bastian Christianbar before the night shift. Bastian Christianbar folded it small and kept it close. Hill 304 is in Hegemony hands. Bastian Christianbar stopped arguing about the next watch and went to check the stores.
The medics cleaned Bastian Christianbar's wound one last time and pronounced him fit. He is back to full duty at S-F1.
At Blackwater Canal, Bastian Christianbar of the Concord and Emil Potato of the Hegemony spent the morning shooting at the same loose sheet of metal. The sheet kept winning.
Bastian Christianbar gave Karel Adauto the last match in the trench. Karel used it to light a candle so that Bastian could finish a letter.
Bastian Christianbar's spoon vanished during supper. He scratched a mark into a replacement and began keeping a closer eye on the washing bucket.
Blackwater Canal is lost. Bastian Christianbar heard the news from a runner, said nothing, and checked his rifle twice. There will be another race.

A second spoon disappeared. Bastian Christianbar searched the washing area and found a gap behind the board where everyone left cutlery to dry. The clerk counted the names twice. Bastian Christianbar is number 353 of the first thousand to answer the call, and wears the ribbon of the First Thousand. News of the loss of Grey Mill reached S-F1 with the rations. Bastian Christianbar ate while listening to the revised orders.
On sentry duty Bastian Christianbar watched the wire for six hours. Twice he thought the wire watched back.
Bastian Christianbar lifted the board. The gap contained seven spoons, a button and a pencil people had blamed the quartermaster for losing.
davitorresg: Nobody saw Norbert Davitorresg arrive. One morning there was simply one more helmet in N-F10, and a quiet machine gunner under it. The sergeant read out the order: Grey Mill has fallen, hold the line. Norbert Davitorresg looked at the new recruits coming up the road and counted them.

A flare lit the Sunken Road like noon. Norbert Davitorresg counted the seconds until darkness: eleven. A letter from home reached Norbert Davitorresg before dusk. Norbert Davitorresg read it twice and slept a little easier.

Norbert Davitorresg and Hugo Dbd both swear they saw a ghost at Sorrow Copse. Each says the other screamed first. A letter from home reached Norbert Davitorresg before dusk. Norbert Davitorresg read it twice and slept a little easier.
dravci85: Bram "Ghost" Dravci took the place of a man nobody would talk about. The dugout still had his blanket. He kept it folded.
The First Wave ribbon marked Bram "Ghost" Dravci as an early volunteer. At S-F14, a newcomer asked what those first days had been like.
Day 3: Verdel Ridge was lost. Bram "Ghost" Dravci wrote down the news without trying to explain it.
Bram "Ghost" Dravci watched a pale shape beyond the wire while a flare burned out. It turned out to be a sack, right where the sack had always been.
Bram "Ghost" Dravci sorted the dressings by lamplight. When the next stretcher arrived, he could find everything without looking.

Bram "Ghost" Dravci opened a parcel addressed in unfamiliar handwriting. A note inside said the usual writer had hurt a wrist. He read that note first. Hill 304 has been won. Bram "Ghost" Dravci listened as the corporal read the news twice, once for the men just off watch.
Bram "Ghost" Dravci ended a letter with 'nothing to report', then added half a page about the missing soap.
A bullet found Bram "Ghost" Dravci at S-F14, high in the shoulder. He went down hard and stayed down. Shot by Clement Tsanev of the Concord (@vl.tsanev).
A medic stopped by Bram "Ghost" Dravci's stretcher every few hours for a week. Today the medic found it empty. Bram "Ghost" Dravci had gone back to S-F14.

Bram "Ghost" Dravci was hit in the hand while passing a mug along the trench at S-F14. He did not spill a drop. The men are still talking about that. Shot by Tobias "Crow" Cowboii of the Concord (@the_cowboii).

Bram "Ghost" Dravci returned to S-F14 with a fresh bandage and orders to keep it dry. He has already broken the second part. The Hegemony took Blackwater Canal, and the orders at S-F14 changed before the cheering ended. Bram "Ghost" Dravci shouldered another load.

Bram "Ghost" Dravci was made Lance Corporal after keeping the section together under fire. He asked that the rest of the section be mentioned too. Bram "Ghost" Dravci walked the captured trenches of Grey Mill and found the enemy's cooking pots still warm. He took a spoon as a souvenir.
An empty jam tin became Bram "Ghost" Dravci's cup. The first drink still tasted of strawberries. He took small sips.
Bram "Ghost" Dravci's spoon vanished during supper. He scratched a mark into a replacement and began keeping a closer eye on the washing bucket.
earn_e: On Day 11, Konrad Earn arrived during an argument about a missing spoon. The war already had matters more urgent than introductions. Konrad Earn was named Hero of Grey Mill. Asked for a few words, he gave the names of the people who had helped.
A bullet hit Konrad Earn's belt buckle at P-F2 and glanced off into his side. Shallow, the medic said. He is keeping the buckle. Shot by Anselm Chandlerz of the Concord (@the_skyler_of_chandlerz).

A round came through the loophole Konrad Earn was watching at P-F2 and hit him in the collarbone. He is alive and very angry. Shot by Oskar Kyamites of the Concord (@kalamitous_kyamites). Konrad Earn was killed outright at P-F2, a single bullet from across the wire. Shot by Oskar Kyamites of the Concord (@kalamitous_kyamites).
The House of Earn sent Silas Earn after Konrad Earn. This time the family packed two pairs of spare socks.
jake_watt1236: Yann Watt came up with a draft of replacements on Day 10. Nobody asked his name until the third night. After that, everyone knew it.

Yann Watt took the shot at four hundred yards. The spotter whispered the result: Roland "Saint" Thedukeofvel, gravely wounded. Word came down the line: Grey Mill is ours. Yann Watt shook hands with a corporal he had never spoken to. Today, everyone was a friend.
Yann Watt warmed the ink bottle inside his tunic. The letter began only when the ink agreed to move.
Yann Watt tried to write home with gloves on. The address is readable. Everything else will need some imagination.
nicolassuess: Benedikt Nicolassuess arrived with the Day 9 draft, carrying a tin whistle and the news from home, which was old by the time he told it.
Day 10. The Hegemony took Blackwater Canal. From the heights Benedikt Nicolassuess could see the whole Concord line, and for the first time the war looked winnable.

A sniper's bullet hit Benedikt Nicolassuess at S-R14. The medics worked on him in the bottom of the trench and shouted for a stretcher. Shot by Jonas Ybarry of the Concord (@ilovturnip28ybarry). A single shot at S-R14. Benedikt Nicolassuess sat down against the trench wall as if to rest, and did not get up. Shot by Jonas Ybarry of the Concord (@ilovturnip28ybarry).

The papers say Jonas Nicolassuess. The sergeant says he has his brother's eyes. Benedikt Nicolassuess's eyes. Nobody in S-R14 argues. Grey Mill has been won. Jonas Nicolassuess listened as the corporal read the news twice, once for the men just off watch.
Jonas Nicolassuess's hands still remember being a bookbinder's hands. Today they mended a broken duckboard as if it were the most important job in the world.
Bastian Ale and Jonas Nicolassuess carved a chessboard into an ammunition box. The pieces are bullets, buttons and one very patient beetle.
shiniestmeatbicycle05: Felix "Mud" Shiniestmeat arrived on Day 11 as a replacement. The men in U-F17 had been fighting for 11 days already and looked at his clean boots like a rumour from another world. The Hegemony secured Grey Mill. Felix "Mud" Shiniestmeat helped pass the news along the line, checking each time that he had heard correctly.
A grenade burst short of the parapet at U-F17. Felix "Mud" Shiniestmeat took a splinter in the hand and was bandaged where he stood.
The medic looked at Felix "Mud" Shiniestmeat's wound, sniffed it, and sent him back to U-F17. Clean, said the medic. It is the best word a medic knows.
thecommanderrod: The new signaller gave his name as Dorian Thecommander. The corporal looked at his boots, then at the mud, and laughed for the first time in a week. Dorian Thecommander asked to leave the signallers and serve as a stretcher bearer. The sergeant looked at him for a long time, then signed the paper without a word.

Dorian Thecommander tried to write neatly for the first line of a letter. By the third, he was writing as quickly as the thoughts arrived. A letter from home found Dorian Thecommander before the night shift. Dorian Thecommander folded it small and kept it close. Grey Mill fell to the Hegemony. Dorian Thecommander kept the newspaper; he wanted to remember exactly what had been promised beforehand.
Quentin Adams owes Dorian Thecommander so many cigarettes that they stopped counting and started writing it down. The notebook is nearly full.
Dorian Thecommander wrote a letter for Roland Bfitzy's mother, because Roland could not find the words. Roland signed it.
viaenegilles: Pavel Viaenegilles found a place in T-F23 between a snorer and a man who talked in his sleep. The available alternative was under the leak.

Pavel Viaenegilles had watched a loose sandbag in the enemy wall for two days. This morning it moved. Oskar "Bones" Theophane was grazed. A bullet bounced off the trench wall and caught Pavel Viaenegilles across the shin at T-F23. It bled a lot and meant very little. Shot by Pavel "Tin" Jacob of the Concord (@steinhoff.jacob). The report confirmed the Hegemony victory at Grey Mill. Pavel Viaenegilles folded the paper so the headline stayed on the outside.
Back on the fire step at T-F23. Pavel Viaenegilles says the wound itches, which the medics say is a good sign.
At the Hanging Bridge, Pavel Viaenegilles and Isidor Patience exchanged rifle shots until a shell burst between the positions. For a while, both rifles remained silent.
